programs.nl_rule:
In the input, you should see...two gray lines with blue squares on the top and bottom of each.

The output grid size... will only be as big as the gray lines with their blue ends, with all the squares that are in between them. (If you see two gray lines that are 3 squares long, and there is 3 spaces of black space between the two lines, your grid would be 5x5: Make sure to include the blue ends of each gray line in your size calculation.

To make the output, you have to...recreate the position of the black space and any blue squares that are between your gray lines. The four corners of your output will be the blue ends of the gray lines in the input. Make sure that the exact amount of black space between the two lines matches the input, and the placement of any blue squares in the black space also matches the exact location in the input. Your output grid should be no bigger on top/bottom or left/right of the blue squares at the end of each gray line.

content.text:
Let me understand the rule from the verifier.

We have input grid. There are two gray (5) vertical lines, each with blue (8) squares at top and bottom ends.

The output is the subgrid spanning from just outside the top-left corner to just outside the bottom-right corner. Let me trace.

x0 = partition(I) - each color as object
x1 = objects(I, T, F, F) - univalued objects, not diagonal, without_bg=False (so bg=None means... actually without_bg False means bg=None, so all objects including background)

x2 = double height, x3 = equality(double(height), size) - checks object where 2*height == number of cells (i.e., a vertical line)
x4 = double width, x5 = equality(double(width), size) - horizontal line
x6 = either - so object is a line (vertical or horizontal)

x7 = equality with TWO (2)
x8 = colorfilter(x1, color) 
x9 = sfilter(vline)
x10 = sfilter(hline)
x11 = chain(x9, x8, color) - objects of a given color that are vlines
x12 = chain(x7⤙size⤙x11) - size == 2, i.e., 2 vertical lines of that color
x13 = chain(x10, x8, color) - hlines of that color
x14 = size==2
x15 = either(both(x6,x12), ...) actually fork(both, x6, x15) - wait x16 = fork(both, x6, x15) where x15 = fork(either, x12, x14).

So an object (color) satisfies condition if it's a line AND (has 2 vlines OR 2 hlines). Wait but x17 = extract(x0, x16) where x0 = partition(I). partition gives objects grouped by color. So we find the color which forms 2 vertical lines.

The color 5 forms 2 vertical lines. Then x18 = color of that object = 5. x19 = colorfilter(x1, 5) - objects of color 5 in x1. x20 = first(x19). x21 = vline(x20) - true.

x22 = ulcorner(x17) where x17 is the partition object of color 5 - upper left of the gray cells. x23 = lrcorner(x17) - lower right of gray cells.

x24 = branch(x21, UP, LEFT) = UP since vline. x25 = add(x22, UP) = (ulrow-1, ulcol). x26 = branch(..., DOWN, RIGHT) = DOWN. x27 = add(x23, DOWN) = (lrrow+1, lrcol).

x29 = {x25, x27}. x30 = subgrid(x29, I) = crop grid from ulcorner of the patch {x25,x27} with shape.

Wait ulcorner(map(min,...)) of the two points: min of (ulrow-1, lrrow+1) = ulrow-1; min of cols = min(ulcol, lrcol) = ulcol. shape height = (lrrow+1)-(ulrow-1)+1 = lrrow-ulrow+3. Hmm.

Actually the gray line for color 5: columns are 1 and 7. Rows 2 to 10 (0-indexed). ulcorner of gray = (2,1). lrcorner = (10,7).

x25 = (1, 1) (UP). x27 = (11, 7) (DOWN).

subgrid from ulcorner of patch = (1,1), shape = height: max(1,11) - min(1,11) + 1 = 11, width: max(1,7)-min(1,7)+1 = 7.

So crop(I, (1,1), (11,7)). That's rows 1-11? rows 1 to 11 inclusive is 11 rows (1..11). Wait height 11 starting at row1: rows 1..11. Columns 1..7.

Let's check the expected output. The example input rows:

Row0: [0,0,0,0,0,8,0,0,8]
Row1: [0,8,0,0,0,0,0,8,0]
Row2: [0,5,0,0,0,0,0,5,0]
...
Row10:[0,8,0,8,0,0,0,8,0]

The expected output given:
[8,0,0,0,0,0,8],
[5,0,0,0,0,0,5],
... 10 rows
[8,0,8,0,0,0,8]

So output is 10 rows × 7 cols. Hmm. Crop rows 1..11 would be 11 rows. But image is 11 rows (rows 0-10). Crop(1,1,(11,7)) - rows from 1 to 1+11=12, but grid only has 11 rows, so truncates to row 1..10 = 10 rows. Columns 1..8 truncated to 1..7 = 7 cols. So output = rows 1..10, cols 1..7.

Row1 cols1-7: [8,0,0,0,0,0,8] ✓
Row2: [5,0,0,0,0,0,5] ✓
Row10 cols1-7: [8,0,8,0,0,0,8] ✓

Great. So the output is the bounding box of the gray lines plus blue ends, essentially crop. Concretely: the subgrid from one above the top and one to the... wait for vline case: from ulcorner+UP and lrcorner+DOWN. So it's the rectangle spanning rows [top-1, bottom+1] and cols [leftcol, rightcol]. And truncated to grid bounds.

Hmm, but the task says "Your output grid should be no bigger on top/bottom or left/right of the blue squares at the end of each gray line." Hmm. In this example, the blue squares at ends of gray lines are at row1 and row10 columns 1 and 7. The output includes exactly from row1 to row10 and col1 to col7. So it's the bounding box of the blue end squares. Actually the crop from (topgray-1, leftcol) to (bottomgray+1, rightcol) equals the bounding box of the blue squares at ends (since blue squares are exactly at those positions). Actually blue squares at top: (row1, col1) and (row1, col7). At bottom: (row10,col1),(row10,col7). The bounding box of those four blue squares = rows1-10, cols1-7. And crop yields exactly that. Also the black space in between with blue squares is included.

So essentially: find the four blue corner squares, output the subgrid that is their bounding box (i.e., crop the input to that bounding box). But note the crop might include one extra row/col if blue squares... hmm. Let's think: crop is from ulcorner of gray minus 1 in the direction (UP for vline), to lrcorner of gray plus 1 in direction (DOWN). For vertical lines, that's row above top gray and row below bottom gray, same columns as leftmost/rightmost gray cells (gray spans column of the line, single column). So ulcorner gray = (top row of gray, left gray column). Actually ulcorner uses min over all gray cells, so min row = topmost gray row, min col = leftmost gray col. Since gray is two vertical lines, that's fine.

So for vline: crop rows [topmostgray-1, bottommostgray+1], cols [leftgraycol, rightgraycol].

For hline analog: crop rows [topgrayrow, bottomgrayrow], cols [leftgraycol-1, rightgraycol+1].

So the rule: there are two lines (gray 5), each with blue (8) squares at both ends. Output is the bounding box that includes the gray lines plus their blue end squares (one step beyond each end).

Simplification for teaching: Output = crop of input such that the blue squares at the ends of the gray lines form the four corners. Since the blue squares are exactly one beyond each end of gray line.

So x6 true. x12: size of x11 (vlines of color5) == 2 ✓. Good.

Hmm but partition groups by color globally. The blue 8 also is in partition. Let's check color 8: partition object includes all 8s. Its height and width... would not satisfy. Actually there may be blue at ends and scattered blacks... anyway.

tools.description: End teaching and send the student to the exam: they must solve held-out generator inputs (unseen in demonstrations or probes) with the history so far. No further teaching after this.

result.message: Exam started with 10 held-out generator inputs. The student will answer them one at a time with no feedback.
